ai_policy.title: Our Stance on AI
ai_policy.subtitle: // when the discourse around AI matters more than what's made with it
ai_policy.intro_text: On 15 December 2025 we posted about the Glitchmas update in r/protogen. It was removed.
ai_policy.fact_label: What was actually in the post:
ai_policy.fact_text: Not a single generated image. Screenshots of an interface — and one honest line saying AI helps us write the code.
ai_policy.moderation_text: We asked the mods where the AI art was. The answer: programming is an art form too. From there the conversation went like this:
ai_policy.moderator_quote_1: "Programming everything yourself is far more versatile and reliable than whatever slop an ai chatbot can spit out for you."
ai_policy.moderator_quote_2: "I strongly encourage that you reconsider your methods, and hone your own skills."
ai_policy.moderation_outro: Worth pausing here. Rule 7 is about images. The objection was about how we write code. Those are different things, and swapping one for the other stops being moderation — it becomes a personal opinion about someone else's workflow. The funny part: the only AI in that post was our own line saying we use AI. The lesson, apparently, is not to mention it — then there is nothing to object to.
ai_policy.point1_text: It helps us write code faster, dig through unfamiliar bugs and test ideas we would never otherwise get to. The team is small and it saves us months. We have never hidden it — that very post said so in plain text.
ai_policy.point2_title: Images and code aren't the same thing
ai_policy.point2_text: The AI art rule is a good rule — it keeps the feed from filling up with generated images instead of artists' work. We agree with it. But we don't post generated images. We post an interface we designed and built, and code anyone can read.
ai_policy.point3_text: All of ProtoMap is on GitHub — the map, the economy, the cloud functions, the database rules. You don't have to take our word for it.
ai_policy.conclusion_text: We're not arguing with the rule. We're arguing with applying it to something it wasn't written for. ProtoMap carries on — same way, same tools.
ai_policy.disclaimer: Should the mere existence of AI cause you moral distress, visiting this site is not mandatory.

splash_modal.title: TRANSPARENCY PROTOCOL
splash_modal.intro: A brief update on a recent incident with Reddit moderation.
splash_modal.point1: Our announcement post on r/protogen was removed for "AI-assisted content".
splash_modal.point2: The moderators equated "AI assistance in code" with "AI-generated art", which is an absurd interpretation of the rules.
splash_modal.point3: We stand for transparency and modern development tools. ProtoMap is a community project, and its source code is open.
